title: Context-dependent regulatory variants in Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Chen, Ziheng; Liu, Yaxuan; Brown, Ashley R; Sestili, Heather H; Ramamurthy, Easwaran; Xiong, Xushen; Prokopenko, Dmitry; Phan, BaDoi N; Gadey, Lahari; Hu, Peinan; Tsai, Li-Huei; Bertram, Lars; Hide, Winston; Tanzi, Rudolph E; Kellis, Manolis; Pfenning, Andreas R
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文结合MPRA与可解释深度学习模型，系统解析阿尔茨海默病中非编码变异对转录因子基序及调控活性的细胞类型/状态依赖性影响，虽非直接建模TF-DNA复合物，但聚焦TF基序扰动与调控机制，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Noncoding genetic variants underlie many complex diseases, yet identifying and interpreting their functional impacts remains challenging. Late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), a polygenic neurodegenerative disorder, exemplifies this challenge. The disease is strongly associated with noncoding variation, including common variants enriched in microglial enhancers and rare variants that are hypothesized to influence neurodevelopment and synaptic plasticity. These variants often perturb regulatory sequences by disrupting transcription factor (TF) motifs or altering local TF interactions, thereby reshaping gene expression and chromatin accessibility. However, assessing their impact is complicated by the context-dependent functions of regulatory sequences, underscoring the need to systematically examine variant effects across diverse tissues, cell types, and cellular states. Here, we combined in vitro and in vivo massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) with interpretable machine-learning models to systematically characterize common and rare variants across myeloid and neural contexts. Parallel profiling of variants in four immune states in vitro and three mouse brain regions in vivo revealed that individual variants can differentially and even oppositely modulate regulatory function depending on cell-type and cell-state contexts. Common variants associated with LOAD tended to exert stronger effects in immune contexts, whereas rare variants showed more pronounced impacts in brain contexts. Interpretable sequence-to-function deep-learning models elucidated how genetic variation leads to cell-type-specific differences in regulatory activity, pinpointing both direct transcription-factor motif disruptions and subtler tuning of motif context. To probe the broader functional consequences of a locus prioritized by our reporter assays and models, we used CRISPR interference to silence an enhancer within the SEC63-OSTM1 locus that harbors four functional rare variants, revealing its gatekeeper role in inflammation and amyloidogenesis. These findings underscore the context-dependent nature of noncoding variant effects in LOAD and provide a generalizable framework for the mechanistic interpretation of risk alleles in complex diseases.
abstract_zh: 非编码遗传变异是许多复杂疾病的病因基础，但识别和解释其功能影响仍具挑战性。晚发性阿尔茨海默病（LOAD），一种多基因神经退行性疾病，体现了这一挑战。该疾病与非编码变异密切相关，包括富集于小胶质细胞增强子中的常见变异，以及被认为影响神经发育和突触可塑性的罕见变异。这些变异常通过破坏转录因子（TF）基序或改变局部TF相互作用来扰乱调控序列，从而重塑基因表达和染色质可及性。然而，评估其影响因调控序列的上下文依赖性功能而复杂化，凸显了在不同组织、细胞类型和细胞状态下系统检查变异效应的必要性。在此，我们结合体外和体内大规模平行报告基因分析（MPRAs）与可解释的机器学习模型，系统表征了髓系和神经背景下的常见及罕见变异。在体外四种免疫状态和体内三个小鼠脑区中平行分析变异，揭示了个体变异可根据细胞类型和细胞状态上下文差异性地甚至相反地调节调控功能。与LOAD相关的常见变异倾向于在免疫背景下发挥更强效应，而罕见变异在脑背景下表现出更显著影响。可解释的序列到功能深度学习模型阐明了遗传变异如何导致调控活性的细胞类型特异性差异，指出了直接的转录因子基序破坏和基序上下文的微妙调节。为探究我们报告分析及模型优先化位点的更广泛功能后果，我们使用CRISPR干扰沉默了SEC63-OSTM1位点内一个含有四个功能性罕见变异的增强子，揭示了其在炎症和淀粉样蛋白生成中的门控作用。这些发现强调了LOAD中非编码变异效应的上下文依赖性，并为复杂疾病中风险等位基因的机制解释提供了通用框架。
